correctness.rationale: The noncentral 3-cube lemma is proved for all positive coefficients, all nonzero feasible offsets: every edge direction is coordinate-specific; a centered polygon has opposite support edges paired, forcing center coordinate zero for each active axis; three active axes contradict the nonzero plane offset; two active axes imply the third bound is redundant and force dominance. For a four-cube normal with four positive, non-dominant coordinates, the maximal-coordinate supporting facet is an off-center 3-cube section that fails that dominance condition, hence is not centrally symmetric, so the three-polytope cannot be a zonoid. Dominance gives explicit affine-cube graph; zero coordinates produce a centrally symmetric planar polygon times a segment. Diagonal affine invariance proves box version, including equality boundaries. Exact rational checker independently matched all 1295 integer normal tuples 0..5. Finite checks not used to certify the infinite quantifier.

value.rationale: Completes a concrete, source-identified convex-geometric classification question left open in a 2019 study. It provides an exact, efficiently checkable normal-coordinate criterion for all four-dimensional boxes, resolves a nontrivial six-sided-face case that facet counting alone cannot decide, and explains the singular role of normals with a zero coordinate. Not merely a parametric variant or finite computation.
